clue.text: Author having cake without tea

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of 'outside' means the cake wraps round the tea

parts.note: a bun is a small sweet cake
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A writer who eats cake but goes without a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it is the old sense 'outside', so the cake encloses the tea.
explanation.definitionFit: John Buchan was a Scottish novelist, writer of The Thirty-Nine Steps.

clue.text: Pole wanting British POWs assembled inside

indicators.note: 'inside' puts the rearranged prisoners within the British word

parts.note: Brit is short for British

indicators.note: assembled means put together, so the letters of POWs are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A Pole who wants British prisoners of war gathered indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is the spar at a ship's bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowsprit is a spar projecting forward from a ship's bow.

clue.text: Actor and comedian taking part in dance

indicators.note: the comedian takes part inside the dance, so goes within its letters

parts.note: the Charleston is a 1920s dance
a laugh is an amusing person, a joker

explanation.surface: A performer and a comic both joining in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'laugh' here is a fun, joking person.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Laughton was an English stage and screen actor.

clue.text: A poster's oddly showing church features

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of poster's, the first, third and so on

explanation.surface: A placard that strangely displays parts of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: A is used as it stands; only poster's is thinned out.
explanation.definitionFit: Apses are vaulted semicircular recesses, typically at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Song from crazy Rhode Island girl

parts.note: mad means crazy
RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A tune composed by, or about, an unhinged young woman from Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several unaccompanied voices, popular in the Renaissance.

clue.text: Old country bumpkin has picked up light

parts.note: an ass is a fool, a simpleton

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: airy means light, insubstantial

explanation.surface: A country yokel has spotted a light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' suggests the rural bumpkin, but the definition is Old country.
explanation.definitionFit: Assyria was an ancient kingdom of Mesopotamia, a nation of antiquity.

clue.text: Maybe brother and sister extremely raucous when swallowing ecstasy

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the outer letters surround the ecstasy word
extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters of raucous

parts.note: elation is great joy

explanation.surface: Siblings who get very loud after taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ecstasy' suggests the drug but means joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brothers and sisters are kin, examples of family members.

clue.text: County's various resources delight, though not initially

indicators.note: various suggests diverse arrangements, so the letters are mixed up
not initially means the first letter of delight is dropped

explanation.surface: A shire's assorted assets give pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges RESOURCES with ELIGHT, delight without its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloucestershire is an English shire in the west of the country, home of the Cotswolds.

clue.text: Perhaps I could be a permissive sort?

definitions.meaning: the character I is an example of an alphabet symbol
someone who lets others do things, one who allows

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether they are too indulgent.
explanation.definitionFit: I is an alphabet character; one who lets, or allows, is a let-ter.

clue.text: Sound whiny, stitching name into jeans the wrong way

indicators.note: stitching one thing into another sews it inside
into says where the name goes, within the jeans
the wrong way means back to front, so the jeans word is read backwards

parts.note: Levis are a brand of denim jeans

explanation.surface: Complaining while sewing a name label into back-to-front denims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' reverses LEVIS to SIVEL, and N goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To snivel is to whimper or cry tearfully, which is to whine.

clue.text: Is getting very tired — floats were no use when swimming

indicators.note: letters that are swimming move about freely, so the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer exhausted because the buoyancy aids were useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when swimming' signals an anagram of all fifteen letters of FLOATS WERE NO USE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to tire yourself completely through exertion, matching becoming exhausted.

clue.text: Stops son wearing jumper

indicators.note: something wearing a garment has it around it, so the jumper encloses the son

parts.note: in Britain a jumper is a knitted sweater, also called a pullover

explanation.surface: A boy dressed in a woolly sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A British 'jumper' is a sweater, not someone who jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver who pulls over halts at the roadside, so the phrasal verb is a synonym for halts.

clue.text: Handlebar, perhaps, is partly detached

indicators.note: 'partly' means only a part of the word detached is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A handlebar coming loose from a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handlebar' suggests a bicycle, but a handlebar moustache has long curled ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Tache is informal British slang for a moustache, and a handlebar is one style of it.

clue.text: Establish place for animal at rear of home

indicators.note: the stall comes after, behind, the home letters in the answer

parts.note: in means at home
a stall is a compartment for a horse or cow in a stable

explanation.surface: Setting up a pen for livestock behind the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone or something is to set it up or settle it in place, a synonym of establish.

clue.text: Left a fire blazing: this could mean hell!

indicators.note: a blazing fire throws things about wildly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that an unattended fire could end in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hell' is meant literally: one possible destination after death.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell is one possible version of existence after death, as heaven is another.

clue.text: Awaken reveller stripped of outer clothing

indicators.note: the outer letters are the reveller's clothing, so the first and last are taken away

parts.note: a carouser is someone who drinks and makes merry

explanation.surface: A partygoer who has taken off their coat is woken up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse or wake someone from sleep is a synonym for waking them, both verbs.

clue.text: Shape of writing implement with label attached

parts.note: a pen is a tool for writing
a tag is a label
on means attached, as in 'with the lid on'

explanation.surface: The form of a pen bearing a sticker.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagon is a five-sided polygon, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Male against small insect

parts.note: anti means opposed to
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A man opposed to tiny bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying mantis is a predatory insect known for its folded forelegs.

clue.text: Short European woman's more chic

indicators.note: short means cut, with the last letter of the European word removed

parts.note: a Swiss is a person from Switzerland
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A small woman from Europe is more stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of height, but it trims a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal British for smart or fashionable; the comparative means smarter.

clue.text: Ascetic scoffed about American soldiers

indicators.note: 'about' means the eaten word goes around the American

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily
US stands for the United States, so American
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Someone who wolfed food down while discussing US troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' here means devoured, not mocked; RE is the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a severe, self-denying way of life, so they are adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Clever, like pupil missing English at last

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken away
at last says the English letter goes from the end

parts.note: a tutee is a person being tutored

explanation.surface: Smart, as a student would be if not for failing English.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means shrewd and sharp-witted, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Commander visited by corporal finally in hospital

indicators.note: a commander visited by others has them inside the place

parts.note: CIC is short for commander-in-chief

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of corporal

explanation.surface: A commanding officer has a corporal visit him in a military hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a medical facility for outpatients, a kind of small medical centre.

clue.text: Drink in village restaurant

indicators.note: 'in' means the letters sit inside the words village restaurant, across the gap

explanation.surface: Having a beverage at a country eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a pale beer, one example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: During journey, train isn't suffering disruption

indicators.note: letters suffering disruption are thrown out of order, so the words train isn't are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rail traveller's complaint that the service is disrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or people on their way between places are said to be travelling, mid-route.

clue.text: UN official's name in one article after another

indicators.note: 'in' puts the name between the two articles
after means one article follows the other

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
another article, a second an

explanation.surface: A United Nations figure named in successive news pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Kofi Annan was Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1997 to 2006.

clue.text: Japanese drama about fool seeking election still

indicators.note: 'about' means the drama wraps around the fool

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked theatre
a twit is a silly person
a candidate is standing for office

explanation.surface: A clown in a Noh play who is running for office anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' at the end looks like an adverb of the surface, but it is the definition, meaning 'nevertheless'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb meaning nevertheless or all the same, the word is a synonym of still.

clue.text: Is airline able to stray inside part of Aussie location?

parts.note: can means is able to

indicators.note: 'inside' puts the straying word within the airline

parts.note: BA is British Airways
to err is to go astray

explanation.surface: A question about whether an airline can wander off course over Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Canberra is the Australian capital, a city forming part of the country.

clue.text: Translation of a French drama excerpt for the radio

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: words for the radio are heard rather than read, so we want a word sounding like the excerpt

parts.note: a scene is a section of a play

explanation.surface: A French radio play, translated and excerpted.
explanation.walkthrough: An unseen is a school exercise translating a passage not seen before.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools an unseen is a passage set for translation without preparation.
